findings.title: Reconcile 月 sense records with dictionary evidence and review findings
findings.details: The final article still has unresolved sense-status and wording conflicts after four revision rounds. It marks moonlight, monthly, round-form, time-counting-unit, and surname senses historical while reviewers repeatedly said the cited dictionary lists them without establishing that they are obsolete. It also calls 月:calendar_month current while its gloss includes “(historical use),” and its cited current dictionary wording is “each month,” not a calendar-month noun. Current Chinese use of 月 for “moon” is asserted without current-use evidence in the citations. These are actual artifact conflicts; rejected suggestions to change statuses alone do not establish the correct resolution.
findings.verification: Inspect the cited dictionary entry in its target-language context and add evidence for present-day meanings where supported. Otherwise omit or rescope unsupported senses. Align each retained sense’s gloss, status, text, citations and generated has_sense edge; ensure the learner’s current meaning has a supported current sense record. Obtain fresh independent factual and readability reviews of the revised article.

findings.title: Record unresolved 月 research gaps in the dossier
findings.details: The research result documents unresolved issues in word-family proposals, the exact date and mechanism of 月/夕 graphic differentiation, seal-form change, and external Unihan access. The supplied dossier does not show these as research-gap records; the article only includes a general word-family limitation and brief graphic-history qualifications. Preserve these as scoped gaps without implying the questions are settled or that failed access is evidence.
findings.verification: Confirm the final dossier retains the research result’s unresolved items and records applicable gaps with their exact scope and evidence. Keep claims limited to what was inspected; do not upgrade the local Unihan reading or reported source interpretations into independently verified findings.
